results.title: Automakers might start hiking prices to offset tariffs: Dealership exec
results.content:
Toyota, the world's largest automaker by volume, saw net income fall 25% in the first nine months of its fiscal year 2026, according to a filing. Tariffs were a major driver — costing the company about 1.2 trillion yen, or roughly $8 billion.

Toyota told CNBC in an email that the tariffs are "highly disruptive" and "cannot be sustained." The company has 11 U.S. factories — one co-owned with Mazda — where it built about 55% of the vehicles it sold in the country in 2025. [...] Key Points

 The president of one of the largest public auto dealership groups said on an earnings call that tariff costs are becoming unsustainable for automakers
 Manufacturers are likely to start passing costs on to buyers through higher prices or by cutting costs on parts.
 So far, tariffs have had a relatively minor effect on vehicle prices, said one auto analyst, but they still cost major automakers billions in 2025, and many are expecting similar payouts in 2026.
